title: Personal Portfolio Website
description: A personal website built from scratch to showcase my work. It has a responsive layout, a light and dark theme, and project and GitHub data that load from JSON and the GitHub API instead of being hard-coded.
highlights: Navigation menu generated with JavaScript and shared across every page
Theme switcher (automatic, light, dark) that remembers your choice with localStorage
Project cards rendered from a JSON file with a reusable function
Live GitHub profile stats fetched from the GitHub API

title: Green Plate Value Engine
tools: Python, Streamlit, Google Places API, scikit-learn, PyDeck
description: A web app for finding vegetarian-friendly restaurants. Enter a location and it pulls nearby restaurants from the Google Places API, then ranks them with a value score that combines each restaurant's Google rating with plant-based keywords found in its reviews and editorial summaries.
highlights: Interactive map with color-coded restaurant pins
Neighborhood summaries showing typical prices and top picks
Isolation Forest anomaly detection that flags suspicious listings, like very high ratings with very few reviews
Results you can sort by value score, rating, number of reviews, or price

title: Are Explicit Tracks More Popular?
description: An analysis of 5,505 Spotify tracks across five genres, testing whether explicit songs are more popular than non-explicit ones. The project starts with a hypothesis test to see if the popularity gap is real or just chance, then builds a machine learning model that predicts a track's popularity from its features. Finally, it checks whether that model works equally well for explicit and non-explicit songs, or whether it is biased toward one group.
highlights: A permutation test found explicit tracks score 5.06 points higher in popularity on average (p < 0.001)
A Random Forest model predicting popularity reached an F1-score of 0.421, up from 0.332 for the baseline
A fairness check found the model was much more precise for explicit tracks (0.562) than non-explicit ones (0.301)

title: Traveler Insight CLI
tools: Python, DSPy, OpenAI API (gpt-4o-mini), Wikipedia API
description: A command-line tool that helps travelers get to know a destination before they go. You type in a place, and it pulls live Wikipedia articles about it, then uses an LLM to turn them into a short cultural briefing.
highlights: Each briefing has seven sections: cultural etiquette, language and communication, food and dining norms, festivals and holidays, religion and spiritual sites, heritage and monuments, and conversation starters
Uses DSPy to structure the LLM prompts, so every briefing follows the same format
Handles ambiguous place names by detecting when a search matches multiple Wikipedia articles
Lets you look up multiple destinations in one session
